subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: Should explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec warn and continue without PTY, fail fast, or remain documentation-only?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the permanent behavior changes an operator-visible sandbox boundary and maintainers should choose the product/security semantics before another fix PR lands.

options.title: Warn and continue
options.body: Add a user-visible warning when sandbox mode disables PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

options.title: Fail explicit PTY
options.body: Treat `pty: true` as a hard requirement in sandbox mode and return an error instead of running without PTY, accepting the compatibility break for explicit calls.

options.title: Document only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and document the limitation, leaving explicit calls to continue silently at runtime.

recommendation.title: Warn and continue
recommendation.body: Add a user-visible warning when sandbox mode disables PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The PTY support and existing degraded-PTY warning behavior both trace most clearly to this exec feature history.
